newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks lower at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks lower at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were lower with bonds at midday Tuesday as profit-taking came into the market after a two-day bounce.
The Dow industrials were down 12 points at 6544, and declines led advancing issues by a narrow margin. Volume was about 216 million shares.
"Typically, when a market starts to rally from its lows, the first rally is not a very good one. That's standard procedure," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.
Around midday, the Dow began to climb off its lows, as did the Nasdaq Composite index, a barometer of high tech stocks. Nasdaq was up fractionally at 1252.

"We have not made a bottom; we had a trading low," Blumberg said. "This is a recovery which will last a few days, but not more than that. It's led by techs, and usually after a correction like the one they have had, you rotate into another group. I think we will re-test the lows next week."
High techs have led the rebound since Friday and received further impetus from better-than-forecast earnings at Advanced Micro Devices Inc.
Advanced Micro was up 2-1/2 at 43-3/4. Intel Corp was up 5/8 at 145-3/4, Microsoft Corp was up 9/16 at 145-11/16, and International Business Machines Corp was up 2-3/4 at 135.

"The worst is probably over for the techs, but this is not the group that will lead us higher," Blumberg said. "That will be the role of either the consumer non-durables or energy stocks. People tend to get defensive after a sell-off, and consumer non-durables have earnings consistency and the energy sector has gotten washed out."
Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons, said the techs remain the best bet for long-term investors.

"The techs are saying that they are the place to be in a bounce. Long-term investors are chasing earnings, and I don't know of any group that has better earnings prospects for the remainder of this decade," Goldman said.
He said the market was undergoing a bounce from its lows and would move up another 100 to 125 points.
"The important thing is that we are still seeing a correction in a bull market," he said.
Motorola Inc fell 5/8 to 59-5/8 despite surpassing first quarter earnings estimates. Analysts said the company's outlook was positive but cautious.
Transocean Offshore Inc was up 2-1/2 at 61-3/8. The company said it had received letters-of-intent to contract the Transocean Rather and Transocean Driller, two of its modern deepwater drilling rigs.
Viking Office Products Inc fell 5-1/2 to 14-1/2 after forecasting third quarter earnings below Wall Street estimates.
